 Coram:Honourable Mr. Justice Divyesh A. Joshi
 Date : 06/03/2026
Oral Order

1. By way of preferring present petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, petitioners have prayed for the following main relief/s:
"A. This Hon'ble Court be pleased to admit and allow this Special Civil Application.
B. This Hon'ble Court may be pleased to quash and set aside the impugned order dated 27.11.2024 passed by the respondent No.2, at Annexure-A, cancelled the application from the register and filed/daftar the application made by the petitioners dated 28.06.2018 annexed at annexure 'D' qua land situated at village Magdalla,
Taluka: Choriyasi, District: Surat, bearing survey No.43/4, admeasuring 5700 square Jyantibhai Keshabhai Alias Keshavbhai ... vs The State Of Gujarat on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122724589/
1 meters by way of issuing suitable writ, order or direction under Article 226 of India.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/17983/2025 ORDER DATED: 06/03/2026 undefined C.

This Hon'ble Court may be pleased to direct the respondent No.2 to allow the application made by the petitioners dated 28.06.2018 annexed at annexure 'D' to the present petition qua acquired land of the petitioners situated at village Magdalla,
Taluka: Choriyasi, District:
Surat, bearing survey No.43/4, admeasuring 5700 square meters and make payment of compensation accordingly to the petitioners, by way of issuing suitable writ, order or direction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India."

2. Learned advocate Mr. Sheth appearing for the petitioners submits that petitioners were the owners and occupiers of land bearing Survey No.43/4, admeasuring 9500 Sq. Mtrs., situated at village Magdalla, Taluka Choryasi, District Surat, which are acquired for the purpose of expansion of Surat (Gavier) Airstrip.
On 22.03.1999, first proposal was made by the respondent No.3 for acquisition of various parcels of land of the concerned claimants including 3800 sq. meters of land of the petitioners.

However, adjoining lands including 5700 sq. mtrs. of land of the present petitioners were left out and therefore second proposal was made on 31.03.1999 for acquisition of lands of left out claimants including the present petitioners.
Thereafter, a notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act (it shall hereinafter be referred to as the 'Act' for short) was published in Government Gazette on 01.04.1999.
Thereafter, a notification under Section 6 of the Act came to be published in the Government Gazette on 15.06.1999.

He submits that the Land Acquisition NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/17983/2025 ORDER DATED: 06/03/2026 undefined Officer passed award on 22.06.2001 awarding the amount of compensation at the rate of Rs.17/- per sq. mtr. for the acquired land.
He submits that being aggrieved by the said order, some of the claimants have filed reference before the Reference Court for enhancement of the compensation.
The Reference Court partly allowed the said reference by determining the market value of the acquired land at the rate of Rs.203.50.

3. Learned advocate Mr. Sheth for the petitioners further submits that the petitioners had not filed the reference under Section 18 of the Act and therefore after the Award came to be passed by the Reference Court, the petitioners preferred an application under Section 28A of the Act before the Respondent No.2 - Special Land Acquisition Officer.
Thereafter, the respondent No.2 sent the draft award to the respondent No.1 for approval.

He submits that surprisingly the respondent No.2 passed the impugned order dated 27.11.2024, whereby the application preferred by the petitioners under Section 28A of the Act came to be filed and case has been de-registered on the ground that the land of the present petitioners is not included in the notification issued under Section 4 of the Act on 23.03.1999, wherein, various parcels of land of other claimants are included and the Reference Court has passed the Award under Section 18 of the Act qua those claimants.
He submits that the said view adopted by NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/17983/2025 ORDER DATED: 06/03/2026 undefined the respondent No.2 is not legal and valid.

He submits that the first preliminary notification under Section 4 of the Act for acquisition of certain parcels of land (i.e. the land for which the Reference Court has enhanced the amount of compensation) was published on Jyantibhai Keshabhai Alias Keshavbhai ... vs The State Of Gujarat on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122724589/
2 23.03.1999, whereas another preliminary notification under Section 4 of the Act for acquisition of the land of the petitioners and other claimants was published on 31.03.1999 and in both the cases i.e. the land of the other claimants in whose favour the Reference Court has passed the award under Section 18 of the Act as well as the land of the petitioners, the notification under Section 4 of the Act came to be published in the Government Gazette on the same day i.e. on 01.04.1999.

sentences.text: Thus, instead of considering the date of publication of notification in the Government Gazette, the respondent No.2 has considered the date of issuance of preliminary notification under Section 4 of the Act.

The said view adopted by the authority concerned is not legal and valid and merely on the said ground,
the application of the petitioners ought not to have been filed by the concerned authority.
4. Learned advocate Mr. Sheth further submits that it is settled proposition of law that the authority concerned has to treat similarly situated persons equally.

He submits that in the instant case, it seems that at the time of deciding the application preferred by the petitioners, different yardstick has NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/17983/2025 ORDER DATED: 06/03/2026 undefined been used by the authority concerned and the said fact is clearly found out from the materials and documents available on record.

He has produced a copy of the application preferred under Section 28A of the Act by another villager, wherein, the authority concerned had forwarded different proposal to the concerned Government Authority.
Thus, admittedly, the authority concerned has treated two similarly situated persons differently.

He, therefore, submits that without there being any fault on the part of the petitioners, they have to approach before this Court and therefore the petition may be allowed by imposing suitable cost upon the erring officer.

5. Learned AGP Ms. Surbhi Bhati for the respondent - State has objected present petition with vehemence and submitted that two different notifications under Section 4 of the Act for two different parcels of land have been published and since the land of the petitioners is not included in the notification issued under Section 4 of the Act for acquisition of land of other claimants in whose favour the Reference Court has passed the Award and enhanced the amount of compensation, the authority concerned has passed the impugned order.

However, she has fairly conceded that both the preliminary notifications under Section 4 of the Act for acquisition of land of the other claimants in whose favour an Award under Section 18 of the Act came to be passed by the Reference Court as well as for acquisition of land of the petitioners NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/17983/2025 ORDER DATED: 06/03/2026 undefined and other claimants were published in the official gazette on the same day i.e. on 01.04.1999 and the authority concerned has treated two similarly situated persons in different manner
, an appropriate order may be passed.

6. Having heard learned advocates appearing for both the parties and having gone through the materials, it is found out that petitioners were the owners and occupiers of land bearing Survey No.43/4, admeasuring 9500 Sq. Mtrs., situated at village Magdalla, Taluka Choryasi, District Surat,
which are acquired for the purpose of expansion of Surat (Gavier) Airstrip.
On 22.03.1999, first proposal was made by the respondent No.3 for acquisition of various parcels of land including land admeasuring 3800 sq. mtrs. of the petitioners.

However, adjoining lands including 5700 sq. mtrs. of land of the present petitioners were left out and therefore second proposal was made on 31.03.1999 for acquisition of land of left out claimants including the present petitioners.

Thereafter, notification Jyantibhai Keshabhai Alias Keshavbhai ... vs The State Of Gujarat on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122724589/
3 under Section 4 of the Act for acquisition of various parcels of land including the land of the petitioners was published in the Government Gazette on 01.04.1999.

sentences.text: Thereafter, a notification under Section 6 of the Act came to be published in the Government Gazette.

Thereafter, the Land Acquisition Officer passed award dated 22.06.2001, whereby, he has awarded an amount of compensation at the rate of Rs.17/- per sq. mtr. for NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/17983/2025 ORDER DATED: 06/03/2026 undefined the acquired land.
Being aggrieved by the said order, some of the claimants have filed reference before the Reference Court for enhancement of the compensation.
The Reference Court partly allowed the said reference by determining the market value of the acquired land at the rate of Rs.203.50.

It is found out from the record that the petitioners had not filed the reference before the Reference Court and therefore after the Award came to be passed by the Reference Court, the petitioners preferred an application under Section 28A of the Act before the Respondent No.2 - Special Land Acquisition Officer for enhancement of the compensation.
Thereafter, the respondent No.2 sent draft award to Respondent No.1 for approval.

However, thereafter, the respondent No.2 passed the impugned order dated 27.11.2024,
whereby, the application preferred by the petitioners under Section 28A of the Act came to be filed and case has been de-registered on the ground that the land of the present petitioners is not included in the notification issued under Section 4 of the Act on 22.03.1999, wherein, the parcels of land of other claimants are included and the Reference Court has passed the Award under Section 18 of the Act qua those claimants.

It is pertinent to note that the notification under Section 4 of the Act has been published in the Government Gazette on the same day i.e. on 01.04.1999 for both the parcels of land i.e. the parcels of land in which the Award under section 18 of the Act has been passed by the Reference Court NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/17983/2025 ORDER DATED:
06/03/2026 undefined as well as the land of the present petitioners.

Thus, the authority concerned has committed grave error in filing/de-registering the application of the petitioners on the ground that the land of the petitioners is not included in the notification issued under Section 4 of the Act,
which is considered by the Reference Court for enhancement of the amount of compensation in the matter of other claimants.
It is also pertinent to note that the concerned authority has treated two similarly situated persons in a different manner and the said fact is clearly found out from the record.
7. In view of the aforesaid discussion, the petition stands allowed.
The impugned order passed by the concerned authority is hereby set aside.

The respondent No.2 is directed to take decision on the application preferred by the petitioners under Section 28A of the Act, in accordance with law and as expeditiously as possible and preferably within a period of 8 weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order, keeping in mind the aforesaid observations made by this Court.
